rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Imagination, Nature, and Demystifying Spirituality", "body": "Chance described the imagination as a perceptual mode and a portal to the realm of potential, and said the world a person lives in is limited by what that person can imagine is possible. He contrasted love, which he said nurtures potential, with fear, which he said boils everything down to one way. He explained that his goal on InnerVerse was to remove fear, victim mentality, and appeals to authority from spirituality, and to ask what mythology can say about nature. Pat asked why returning people to nature mattered so much to him."}, {"title": "Middlemen, Source, and the Language of Symbols", "body": "Chance described institutions as systems that place a middleman between people and their source, and he named religious authorities, bankers, food manufacturers, and doctors as his examples. He suggested growing your own food and tending your own health as ways to perceive the source directly. He argued that reclaiming the knowledge of symbolism lets people see what myths say about nature, which he said turns confusing systems into something empowering. He credited Dylan Saccoccio's work for much of this framework, and Pat agreed that learning symbols made the world feel less frightening."}, {"title": "Dylan's Books and Learning Old Alphabets", "body": "Chance said he narrated the third audiobook in Dylan Saccoccio's Spirit Whirled series and was about seventy percent through the fourth. He recommended pairing the ebook, which works as an index, with the audiobook so readers hear how foreign words are pronounced. Chance described learning the Greek and Hebrew alphabets as quick and rewarding, and he offered Thrace and the figure Zalmoxis as examples of connections he noticed in names. Pat said that hearing words pronounced had already made a difference in his own reading."}, {"title": "Learning Biofield Tuning From Eileen Day McKusick", "body": "Chance explained that he wanted to bring sound work to the P.A.T. Life community, mainly so listeners would try it themselves rather than become clients. He held up Eileen Day McKusick's books, Tuning the Human Biofield and Electric Body, Electric Health, and said he learned by reading them and experimenting with forks over a year or two. He said the method was replicable and consistent from person to person. He described a weighted fork that helped a shoulder injury within days. Pat mentioned that he owned a sonic slider."}, {"title": "Injury as Message and the Biofield Explained", "body": "Chance described his belief that injuries and diseases carry an emotional or energetic component, and that events reflect a person's energy communicating back to them. He said the right shoulder related to carrying work and saying yes to others, and the left to absorbed emotional weight. He described the biofield as an aura extending about six feet from the body, and he presented attachment and possession as separated parts of the self, a daimon, rather than the only possible explanation. He tied this to the idea of the I am."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I sat down with Pat Daly on the P.A.T. Life podcast to talk about using tuning forks and sound to balance the human biofield, along with the language and symbolism work behind InnerVerse. We also got into how this practice has shaped my own path.

It is a part of this perfect design and this ever-changing design, and you're going, man, I'm in it, I'm a part of it, I'm not separate from it.", "author": "Pat Daly", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "What's important is the modality itself is effective. It's consistent from human to human.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Everything happens as a reflection and an expression and a communication from your energy back to you.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We all have this thing that has been called an aura and it extends on average about six feet off the body in all directions.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I think most people's experience of attachment or possession type energy or entities, like bad voices in their head, is their own energy that they've separated from themselves, compartmentalized somewhere in their biofield.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I'm glad it actually took longer than I originally wanted it to, because it was that time in between where connections were made, ideas came to me that I didn't have originally that made the story better.", "author": "Pat Daly", "portrait": ""}]
